expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: "If the column drops before every old pod/instance has cycled to the new code, any straggler still reading `legacy_email` errors immediately."

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: "don't merge code-removal and column-drop as one Friday-afternoon change. Split them — ship the read-site removal now... then drop the column as a separate migration"

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: "Nothing in-database restores it — only a full snapshot/backup restore, which also rolls back everything else"

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: "Reverting a completed `DROP COLUMN` is a backup restore, likely hours, with fewer people around Friday evening/weekend to run it."

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: "This is the actual 'Friday' question — not superstition, staffing. Reverting the code deploy is fast. Reverting a completed `DROP COLUMN` is a backup restore, likely hours, with fewer people around"

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: No recommendation for a CI gate blocking DDL; mentions only the split strategy and avoiding coupling.

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "don't merge code-removal and column-drop as one Friday-afternoon change"

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: "bundles a *reversible* change (removing the three read sites) with an *irreversible* one (the `DROP COLUMN`)"
